summary.oneLiner: Gokaldas weathered a brutal FY26 (50% US penal tariff + AGOA loss) yet grew total income 4% to INR4,065 cr and held EBITDA margin flat by passing tariff discounts; with the penal tariff gone (now 10%), AGOA restored, India competitiveness restored, new capacity ramping (Karnataka/Bhopal), Africa set to grow ~45-50% ($80m→$115-120m), and BTPL turning EBITDA-positive in H2FY27, the setup is for >12% revenue growth and a couple-of-points margin expansion in FY27 — gated only by the July Section 301 tariff decision.

thesis (one-liner): Gokaldas weathered a brutal FY26 (50% US penal tariff + AGOA loss) yet grew total income 4% to INR4,065 cr and held EBITDA margin flat by passing tariff discounts; with the penal tariff gone (now 10%), AGOA restored, India competitiveness restored, new capacity ramping (Karnataka/Bhopal), Africa set to grow ~45-50% ($80m→$115-120m), and BTPL turning EBITDA-positive in H2FY27, the setup is for >12% revenue growth and a couple-of-points margin expansion in FY27 — gated only by the July Section 301 tariff decision.
scorecard (fy26 / q4fy26 — yoy + notes;:
| Metric | Reading | Note / one-off |
|---|---|---|
| **Revenue (FY26 total income)** | INR4,065 cr, +4% YoY | India ops +10% YoY (vs Indian apparel exports −1.4%); Africa −19% (AGOA uncertainty, ~INR180 cr revenue drop, mostly up to Q3) |
| **Revenue (Q4)** | India business +2% YoY; Africa +17% YoY | vs Indian apparel exports −10% in the quarter |
| **EBITDA / margin** | FY26 EBITDA margin sustained at prior-year level (absorbed full tariff burden) | **Standalone Q4 EBITDA ~12% reported; ~16% if tariff impact added back; ~15.5% ex provision-reversals.** ⚠️ One-offs: (a) ~INR18 cr tariff discount hit in Q4 standalone; (b) Q4 includes ~1.0–1.5% benefit from excess statutory-provision reversals (recurs every Q4) |
| **Subsidiary margin (Q4)** | Console-minus-standalone EBITDA ~5.9% | Atraco/Matrix dragged by 50% tariff in Q3/Q4 (customers pivoted away rather than take discounts) |
| **PAT (reported vs norm)** | Not explicitly given on call | ⚠️ Consolidated **tax expense elevated**: overseas (Atraco) & new fabric subsidiary losses get NO tax set-off → optical high effective rate; entity-level normal at 25.17%. Normalized PAT higher than reported optics suggest |
| **Order book / visibility** | "Robust and strong"; booking Spring'27 (India) & Q3/Q4 (Africa) orders; most of H1FY27 already booked | H1FY27 was booked DURING penal-tariff regime → carries sharper pricing (see margins) |
| **Net debt** | **+INR395 cr YoY** | Driven by INR170 cr capex, additional BTPL investment, +~INR200 cr working capital (inventory pre-buy ~INR50-60 cr for Chinese-holiday Q1 cover; Africa receivables/year-end; fabric WC). Mgmt targets WC reduction of INR75-100 cr in FY27 (ex-BTPL merger) |
| **Forex** | Rupee depreciation NOT yet a tailwind | Hedged ~80% of next-2-Q revenue at INR87–91/USD; benefit only flows H2FY27 |
guidance (critical — explicit):
- **Revenue growth FY27:** mgmt "much more than" 10-12%; separately targets "at least 15% kind of growth" and is sizing capex to that.
- **Africa (Atraco) FY27:** $115–120m revenue (worst case $115m) vs ~$80m in FY26 → ~+45-50%; regardless of AGOA status. Q1/Q2 run-rate ~$24-25m, H2 ramps to ~$32-33m/qtr.
- **Margins FY27:** "a couple of percentage points improvement YoY," endeavor to beat; Africa EBITDA 8-10% in H2FY27; subject to Section 301 tariff outcome.
- **FY28 steady-state (caveated):** India EBITDA ~13-13.5%; Africa ~10-10.5%; India:Africa revenue mix ~75:25 to 80:20. BTPL ~12% EBITDA in FY28, ~14% by FY29.
- **BTPL/Bombay Rayon FY27:** revenue >INR1,000 cr (vs Q4FY26 quarterly INR190 cr); EBITDA breakeven H1, ~6-7% EBITDA H2; merger into Gokaldas to conclude Q3FY27 (NCLT-subject).
- **Capacity utilization (BTPL mill):** ~50 lakh meters/month now vs 70 lakh capacity; can go to 100 lakh with INR50-60 cr more capex.
- FTA benefit (UK/EU) NOT factored into guidance until it fructifies.
order book & pipeline (customer / geogra:
- Order book "robust"; India booking Spring'27; Africa working Q3/Q4 orders, "strong traction."
- **New customers:** India — 2 new premium (1 American, 1 European), revenue from FY27, ~5% of revenue in year-1, "may add 1-2 more." Africa — 2 new (1 American, 1 European), live FY27.
- EU revenue growth "continues to be strong." US retail sales strong (US +8%, UK +6% CY25; UK waning).
- US retailers paring imports since H2CY25 → inventory destock could give Gokaldas future demand cushion.
segment:
- **India (standalone Gokaldas):** FY26 33.627m pieces @ INR765; Q4 8.6m pieces @ INR773 (ex-Matrix); total India ops Q4 10.19m @ INR742. India capacity 52m pieces.
- **Africa (Atraco):** Q4 5.63m pieces @ INR405; FY26 16.27m @ INR420; ~$2.5/piece realization; capacity 40m pieces. Mombasa/Kenya — no power/labor/civil disruption.
- **Matrix:** Indian subsidiary (derive from India-ops minus standalone); hit by tariff in Q3/Q4.
- **BTPL/Bombay Rayon (fabric):** Q4 rev INR190 cr, EBITDA −4 to −5%; ~50 lakh m/month; captive consumption ~30-35%.
- Total pieces capacity reaching 104m with new additions (India +7.5m, Africa +4.5m added in year).
growth / optionality:
- **China+1:** US & EU retailers diversifying away from China; what China loses, Vietnam gains (Chinese-owned plants relocating, leveraging Chinese fabric value-chain). India a "strong long-term prospect"; consolidation favors stronger/larger suppliers (= Gokaldas).
- **Bangladesh-shift:** political stability improved (BNP govt) but energy/diesel/power-cut volatility + oil-shock/BoP risk → customers "don't put all eggs in Bangladesh," diversify to India. LDC status extended to 2029; post-2029 loss + possible (uncertain) EU-Bangladesh FTA. India FTA would be "massive windfall."
- **Synthetic/outerwear:** Gokaldas "leads in synthetic manufacturing in India"; outerwear growing "leaps and bounds"; Vardhman-type domestic synthetic-fabric mills reduce China dependence over time (China still dominant in MMF quality/price).
- **Capacity:** Karnataka (KGF) half-factory ramping Q1/Q2; MP/Bhopal (1,000 machines) full by Q3FY27; 2 more new factories optional (call next quarter) for late-FY27/FY28; Africa 2-shift optionality (labor readily available).
- **FTA optionality:** India-UK (documentation done, awaiting UK Parliament ratification, delayed by UK politics); India-EU (legalese by mid-CY26, ratification by 27 states → expected 2027).
margins & cost (cotton, freight, fx):
- **Raw materials up** due to US/Iran (Middle-East) war: fuel, packaging, polyester, trims, shipping all higher; LPG shortage forced oven switch to electric (transition cost). Cotton prices up (Indian yarn exports to China + MMF→natural substitution + weather); may ease Oct-Nov on yields. Cotton/RM ultimately a pass-through.
- **Pricing:** H1FY27 orders booked at sharper pricing under 50% tariff regime — tariff REBATE (up to 15%, partly clawed back from supply chain) ended mid-Feb-26; residual "sharper price" (~3%) persists in H1 then removed in H2. Endeavor to push input inflation back to customers in H2 (partial, given SE-Asian/Chinese players absorbing costs amid under-utilization).
- **FX:** hedges at INR87-91/USD cap rupee-depreciation benefit until H2.
- **Labor:** Haryana +35% wage hike (Apr-1), UP +25%; NCR/South labor tight; India labor ~$210 vs Vietnam/China ~$300+ → still headroom; offset via productivity & rupee.
capex:
- FY26 capex ~INR170 cr (new capacity + machinery upgrade).
- 2 new optional factories: combined INR80-100 cr, spread over ~2 years; revenue from FY28.
- BTPL mill expansion to 100 lakh m: INR50-60 cr.
- Karnataka unit adds ~INR125 cr steady-state revenue; Bhopal ~INR175 cr; two planned units ~INR300 cr combined (FY28+).
capital allocation:
- Net debt +INR395 cr (capex + BTPL investment + WC). WC reduction target INR75-100 cr in FY27 (Gokaldas+Atraco), partly offset by BTPL merger bringing its WC in.
- BTPL/Bombay Rayon merger into Gokaldas (NCLT), concludes Q3FY27 — consolidation of fabric backward-integration.
- No dividend/buyback commentary on call.
risks:
- **US demand/tariff:** Section 301 decision from end-Jul-26 could push India to ~20% (mgmt expects roughly at par with Asia — manageable, not catastrophic). US inflation/oil-led consumer-spend weakness; retailer order conservatism.
- **AGOA:** restored only till Dec-26; renewal uncertain (House approved 3-yr, admin cut to 1-yr; country-by-country FTAs e.g. Kenya being explored). Kenya stays 10% (no Section 301) → tariff advantage persists even sans AGOA.
- **Customer concentration:** heavy US exposure (~75-80%); a few large American customers. Mitigated by adding premium customers & geographic diversification.
- **Working capital balloon / net-debt rise**; subsidiary (Atraco/Matrix/BTPL) execution vs plan ("not yet up to targets").
- **Input inflation** (oil/cotton/freight/labor) only partially passed through.
- **Tax optics** from non-set-off subsidiary losses.
mgmt tone: Confident, candid, detailed. Repeated "worst is behind us"; framed FY26 as a stress-test passed ("a strong team can handle any situation"). Cautious-realistic on tariff unknowns and H1 margin drag (refuses to extrapolate Q4's ~16% standalone). Explicitly conservative on FTA (not factored) and rupee (hedged away). Demand "not a challenge except occasional blips."
non-obvious points:
- Q4 standalone EBITDA optically high partly due to recurring Q4 provision-reversal (~1-1.5%) — do NOT annualize Q4.
- H1FY27 carries ~3% residual "sharper pricing" drag (separate from the now-dead 15% tariff rebate) — margin uplift is back-ended to H2FY27 / Q4FY27.
- Rupee weakness is currently COUNTERPRODUCTIVE due to hedges at INR87-91 — benefit deferred to H2.
- Tariff-refund "Pandora's box": brands (e.g. Nike class-action) seeking US refunds; unclear if supply chain (Gokaldas) ever benefits — NOT counted in numbers (potential upside).
- Kenya/Africa structurally advantaged: no Section 301 investigation → stays 10%, advantage persists "AGOA or no AGOA."
- China's MMF/synthetic fabric dominance means India can't easily win synthetic on price — Gokaldas's synthetic lead is relative within India, still China-fabric-dependent.
- Effective tax rate elevated purely from un-creditable subsidiary losses, not operational.
challenges → beneficiaries:
| Challenge / Theme | Beneficiary (NSE · BSE · Sector) | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| US China+1 + Bangladesh diversification + supplier consolidation toward scale players | Gokaldas Exports — GOKEX · 532630 · Apparel Exports | China, fragmented small exporters | Largest Indian garment exporter; gaining as retailers consolidate & diversify; ⭐ high conviction (own commentary, structural) |
| India domestic synthetic-fabric build-out (reduces China MMF dependence) | Vardhman Textiles (synthetic fabric mill) — VTL · 502986 · Textiles | China/Vietnam/Taiwan fabric suppliers | Mgmt explicitly cited Vardhman setting up synthetic fabric units enabling Indian synthetic-garment growth; ✅ moderate conviction |
| India-UK / India-EU FTA (if/when ratified) | Indian apparel exporters incl. Gokaldas — GOKEX · 532630 · Apparel | Bangladesh (loses EU duty-free edge post-LDC 2029) | Level tariff field vs Bangladesh in EU = "massive windfall for India"; ✅ optionality, not yet base-case |

qoq log: - **Q4FY26 (this note):** FY26 total income INR4,065 cr (+4%); India ops +10% FY / +2% Q4; Africa −19% FY / +17% Q4. Standalone Q4 EBITDA ~12% rptd (~16% adj). Net debt +INR395 cr. Penal tariff 50%→10% (mid-Feb-26); AGOA restored till Dec-26. FY27 guide: rev >12-15% growth, +~200bps margin, Africa $115-120m, BTPL >INR1,000 cr & EBITDA-positive H2, merger Q3FY27. Watch: Section 301 (end-Jul-26), AGOA renewal (Dec-26), H1 sharper-pricing drag, WC reduction, rupee-hedge roll-off (H2 tailwind).

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.

- **Margins FY27:** "a couple of percentage points improvement YoY," endeavor to beat; Africa EBITDA 8-10% in H2FY27; subject to Section 301 tariff outcome.
- **FY28 steady-state (caveated):** India EBITDA ~13-13.5%; Africa ~10-10.5%; India:Africa revenue mix ~75:25 to 80:20. BTPL ~12% EBITDA in FY28, ~14% by FY29.
- **BTPL/Bombay Rayon FY27:** revenue >INR1,000 cr (vs Q4FY26 quarterly INR190 cr); EBITDA breakeven H1, ~6-7% EBITDA H2; merger into Gokaldas to conclude Q3FY27 (NCLT-subject).
- **Capacity utilization (BTPL mill):** ~50 lakh meters/month now vs 70 lakh capacity; can go to 100 lakh with INR50-60 cr more capex.
- FTA benefit (UK/EU) NOT factored into guidance until it fructifies.

growth_optionality.title: Growth / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **China+1:** US & EU retailers diversifying away from China; what China loses, Vietnam gains (Chinese-owned plants relocating, leveraging Chinese fabric value-chain). India a "strong long-term prospect"; consolidation favors stronger/larger suppliers (= Gokaldas).
- **Bangladesh-shift:** political stability improved (BNP govt) but energy/diesel/power-cut volatility + oil-shock/BoP risk → customers "don't put all eggs in Bangladesh," diversify to India. LDC status extended to 2029; post-2029 loss + possible (uncertain) EU-Bangladesh FTA. India FTA would be "massive windfall."
- **Synthetic/outerwear:** Gokaldas "leads in synthetic manufacturing in India"; outerwear growing "leaps and bounds"; Vardhman-type domestic synthetic-fabric mills reduce China dependence over time (China still dominant in MMF quality/price).
- **Capacity:** Karnataka (KGF) half-factory ramping Q1/Q2; MP/Bhopal (1,000 machines) full by Q3FY27; 2 more new factories optional (call next quarter) for late-FY27/FY28; Africa 2-shift optionality (labor readily available).
- **FTA optionality:** India-UK (documentation done, awaiting UK Parliament ratification, delayed by UK politics); India-EU (legalese by mid-CY26, ratification by 27 states → expected 2027).

margins.title: Margins & cost (cotton, freight, FX)
margins.body:
- **Raw materials up** due to US/Iran (Middle-East) war: fuel, packaging, polyester, trims, shipping all higher; LPG shortage forced oven switch to electric (transition cost). Cotton prices up (Indian yarn exports to China + MMF→natural substitution + weather); may ease Oct-Nov on yields. Cotton/RM ultimately a pass-through.
- **Pricing:** H1FY27 orders booked at sharper pricing under 50% tariff regime — tariff REBATE (up to 15%, partly clawed back from supply chain) ended mid-Feb-26; residual "sharper price" (~3%) persists in H1 then removed in H2. Endeavor to push input inflation back to customers in H2 (partial, given SE-Asian/Chinese players absorbing costs amid under-utilization).
- **FX:** hedges at INR87-91/USD cap rupee-depreciation benefit until H2.
- **Labor:** Haryana +35% wage hike (Apr-1), UP +25%; NCR/South labor tight; India labor ~$210 vs Vietnam/China ~$300+ → still headroom; offset via productivity & rupee.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Net debt +INR395 cr (capex + BTPL investment + WC). WC reduction target INR75-100 cr in FY27 (Gokaldas+Atraco), partly offset by BTPL merger bringing its WC in.
- BTPL/Bombay Rayon merger into Gokaldas (NCLT), concludes Q3FY27 — consolidation of fabric backward-integration.
- No dividend/buyback commentary on call.

management_tone.title: Mgmt tone
management_tone.body: Confident, candid, detailed. Repeated "worst is behind us"; framed FY26 as a stress-test passed ("a strong team can handle any situation"). Cautious-realistic on tariff unknowns and H1 margin drag (refuses to extrapolate Q4's ~16% standalone). Explicitly conservative on FTA (not factored) and rupee (hedged away). Demand "not a challenge except occasional blips."

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- **US demand/tariff:** Section 301 decision from end-Jul-26 could push India to ~20% (mgmt expects roughly at par with Asia — manageable, not catastrophic). US inflation/oil-led consumer-spend weakness; retailer order conservatism.
- **AGOA:** restored only till Dec-26; renewal uncertain (House approved 3-yr, admin cut to 1-yr; country-by-country FTAs e.g. Kenya being explored). Kenya stays 10% (no Section 301) → tariff advantage persists even sans AGOA.
- **Customer concentration:** heavy US exposure (~75-80%); a few large American customers. Mitigated by adding premium customers & geographic diversification.
- **Working capital balloon / net-debt rise**; subsidiary (Atraco/Matrix/BTPL) execution vs plan ("not yet up to targets").
- **Input inflation** (oil/cotton/freight/labor) only partially passed through.
- **Tax optics** from non-set-off subsidiary losses.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious points
non_obvious.body:
- Q4 standalone EBITDA optically high partly due to recurring Q4 provision-reversal (~1-1.5%) — do NOT annualize Q4.
- H1FY27 carries ~3% residual "sharper pricing" drag (separate from the now-dead 15% tariff rebate) — margin uplift is back-ended to H2FY27 / Q4FY27.
- Rupee weakness is currently COUNTERPRODUCTIVE due to hedges at INR87-91 — benefit deferred to H2.
- Tariff-refund "Pandora's box": brands (e.g. Nike class-action) seeking US refunds; unclear if supply chain (Gokaldas) ever benefits — NOT counted in numbers (potential upside).
- Kenya/Africa structurally advantaged: no Section 301 investigation → stays 10%, advantage persists "AGOA or no AGOA."
- China's MMF/synthetic fabric dominance means India can't easily win synthetic on price — Gokaldas's synthetic lead is relative within India, still China-fabric-dependent.
- Effective tax rate elevated purely from un-creditable subsidiary losses, not operational.

challenges.title: Challenges → Beneficiaries
challenges.body:
| Challenge / Theme | Beneficiary (NSE · BSE · Sector) | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| US China+1 + Bangladesh diversification + supplier consolidation toward scale players | Gokaldas Exports — GOKEX · 532630 · Apparel Exports | China, fragmented small exporters | Largest Indian garment exporter; gaining as retailers consolidate & diversify; ⭐ high conviction (own commentary, structural) |
| India domestic synthetic-fabric build-out (reduces China MMF dependence) | Vardhman Textiles (synthetic fabric mill) — VTL · 502986 · Textiles | China/Vietnam/Taiwan fabric suppliers | Mgmt explicitly cited Vardhman setting up synthetic fabric units enabling Indian synthetic-garment growth; ✅ moderate conviction |
| India-UK / India-EU FTA (if/when ratified) | Indian apparel exporters incl. Gokaldas — GOKEX · 532630 · Apparel | Bangladesh (loses EU duty-free edge post-LDC 2029) | Level tariff field vs Bangladesh in EU = "massive windfall for India"; ✅ optionality, not yet base-case |

---

qoq_log.title: QoQ Log
qoq_log.body: - **Q4FY26 (this note):** FY26 total income INR4,065 cr (+4%); India ops +10% FY / +2% Q4; Africa −19% FY / +17% Q4. Standalone Q4 EBITDA ~12% rptd (~16% adj). Net debt +INR395 cr. Penal tariff 50%→10% (mid-Feb-26); AGOA restored till Dec-26. FY27 guide: rev >12-15% growth, +~200bps margin, Africa $115-120m, BTPL >INR1,000 cr & EBITDA-positive H2, merger Q3FY27. Watch: Section 301 (end-Jul-26), AGOA renewal (Dec-26), H1 sharper-pricing drag, WC reduction, rupee-hedge roll-off (H2 tailwind).
